concept.object: a round glossy toy sun with a warm smiling glow
concept.morph: the sun squashes into an upright rounded rectangle and a single horizontal bar snaps across its middle
concept.hook: 太陽會像果凍一樣被壓扁，中間啪一聲多一橫

promptVersions.conceptZh: 豬探長舉著超大放大鏡辦案，鏡片把他的眼睛放大成爆笑巨眼；他湊得太近撞到太陽，太陽被壓成直立的圓角方塊，脫手的放大鏡橫飛過來「喀」一聲卡進中間變成那一橫，合成「日」。
promptVersions.object: a chubby glossy toy sun ball with a calm smiling face, and a stout cartoon detective pig with an oversized magnifying glass
promptVersions.morph: the sun squashes into an upright rounded rectangle while the flying magnifying glass snaps across its middle and smooths into the single horizontal stroke of 日
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 第一次為「日」補上 prompt。用孩子喜歡的豬探長開場，放大鏡巨眼是笑點，也自然帶出「撞一下→壓扁→橫桿插進來」的因果，不靠老套的果凍登場。語音詞選「生日」，日固定念ㄖˋ、生固定念ㄕㄥ，沒有破音風險。
promptVersions.promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light-cream background. Centered stands a chubby glossy toy sun: a round tangerine ball with a calm smiling face. A stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat and a tiny trench coat waddles in from the left, holding a magnifying glass far too big for him. From 0.6 to 2.2 seconds he leans in to inspect the sun and, seen through the lens, his one eye balloons to a comically enormous size and blinks twice while the rest of him stays small. Hold that silly pose for a beat. At 2.6 seconds he leans one step too close, bonks the sun with the lens rim, and the sun squashes with a soft jelly wobble into an upright rounded rectangle of saturated vermilion. The magnifying glass pops out of his hands, spins once through the air, and snaps horizontally across the middle of that rectangle with a satisfying click, its rim and handle smoothing into one clean straight stroke. The detective pig tips his hat, very pleased with himself, and hops out of frame to the left by 4.6 seconds. By 5.0 seconds the shape has resolved into one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 日 in saturated vermilion, perfectly centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins on all sides, its outer box and single middle bar crisp, straight and clearly separated. From 5.0 to 8.0 seconds the frame holds completely still on 日 with nothing else moving in the shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast but not neon colors, no dark or moody grading. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「日、日、生日」, using the reading ㄖˋ for 日 both times and in the word. Speak the first 日 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 生日 around 5.6 seconds during the still hold, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep the bonk and the click soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not appear as imagery. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 日: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

promptVersions.conceptZh: 「日」像太陽照出暖暖日光，長短手的玩具機器人想遮陽，卻被自己的長手拍肩，轉頭找了半天。
promptVersions.object: A solid orange-red 日 glyph shining warm sunlight beside a boxy toy robot assembled from mismatched parts.
promptVersions.morph: Begin with the complete, correctly formed glyph. Its shape remains fixed while its sunlight motivates the robot’s self-tapping shade gag; the lighting settles into a flat, crisp final reading view.
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 改用完整的「日」直接表現太陽與日光，不再壓扁太陽或拼接筆畫。機器人過長的手繞到背後拍到自己，誤以為有人叫它，最後才把長手折成遮陽棚。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked-off frontal shot. On a light cream background, place one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 日 precisely at center, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use saturated solid orange-red strokes: an upright rectangular enclosure and one straight horizontal middle stroke joining its left and right sides, with two clearly open cream-colored interior spaces. Keep this geometry intact throughout. The glyph acts as a sun, casting gentle warm light toward the lower-left margin without adding rays, a face, or decorations to its strokes.

The sole animated lead is an original boxy toy robot assembled from visibly mismatched parts: a squat turquoise torso, a mustard square head, mismatched toy feet, one stubby arm and one conspicuously long segmented arm. Its personality is earnestly overconfident. Stage it entirely beside the glyph, with enough separation that its gestures never cross the strokes. No additional props or supporting cast.

At the opening, the robot happily basks in the glyph’s sunlight, then squints and attempts to shade its eyes with its stubby arm. The hand cannot reach its forehead; it stretches onto tiptoe and pauses, baffled. Around 1.3 seconds, it confidently swings its much longer arm overhead. The arm overshoots, bends behind its head, and softly taps its own opposite shoulder. The robot immediately swivels its head to investigate; its attached hand follows and taps again, making it turn back with an exaggerated puzzled double-take. Let this tiny chase read clearly rather than spinning rapidly. By 3.3 seconds, the robot spots its own hand, freezes in sheepish recognition, then deliberately folds the long elbow so the broad palm becomes a perfectly useful sunshade above its eyes. It gives one satisfied nod and waddles out through the left edge by 4.7 seconds, still shading itself.

By 4.8 seconds, the directional sunlight has gently settled into even studio illumination. Hold only the crisp, centered 日 completely still through 8.0 seconds, preserving its solid color, clean interior spaces and full margins. Use chunky molded toy materials, soft shadows and bright restrained colors, with no flashing or blown-out highlights.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「日、日、日光」. Pronounce 日 as ㄖˋ throughout. Speak the first 日 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.3 seconds, and 日光 around 5.5 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly visible in the final hold. Use natural pauses and stop after the word. Add only quiet toy-joint creaks and two soft shoulder taps beneath the voice; no music. The vocabulary is audio only. Keep 日 as the only on-screen writing, with no subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks or clutter. Use only the original stylized toy cast and objects described.

promptVersions.conceptZh: 戴尖耳朵、披紅斗篷的小玩具英雄爬上躺平的月亮想倒掛耍帥，結果月亮被他壓得立起來，他咻地滑到底、屁股著地、斗篷蓋住頭；腰帶上兩塊積木這時滑進來卡成中間兩橫，變出「月」。
promptVersions.object: a chunky cream crescent moon toy lying on its back, and a small boxy caped toy robot hero with pointed ears
promptVersions.morph: the crescent tips upright into the two outer strokes while two chunky bricks from the hero’s belt glide in from the left and click into the two short horizontal strokes of 月
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 第一次為「月」補上 prompt。把孩子喜歡的蝙蝠造型英雄做成無品牌的尖耳朵玩具機器人，用「耍帥失敗、滑下來跌坐」當笑點，同時讓月亮被壓得立起來就是形變本身。兩塊積木補中間兩橫，兼顧他喜歡的樂高元素。語音詞「月亮」的月與亮都只有一種讀音。
promptVersions.promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale-lilac background. Centered lies a chunky cream-colored crescent moon toy resting on its back like a little hammock. From 0.4 seconds a small boxy toy robot hero with pointed ears, round friendly eyes and a short red cape struts in, climbs onto the crescent, and strikes an extremely dramatic pose with his cape flaring, trying to hang upside down from the tip. At 2.0 seconds his weight tips the crescent: it swings upright with a slow comic creak until it stands tall as the two outer strokes, and the tiny hero slides all the way down the inside of the curve and lands on his backside with a soft bonk, his cape flopping over his head. He peeks out from under the cape for a beat. At 3.2 seconds two chunky interlocking plastic bricks pop off his utility belt and glide in from the left, clicking into place one above the other inside the crescent to become the two short horizontal strokes. The hero gives a tiny satisfied thumbs-up and hops out of frame to the right by 4.7 seconds. By 5.0 seconds everything has resolved into one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 月 in saturated deep indigo, perfectly centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins on all sides, its long left stroke, hooked right stroke and two inner bars crisp and clearly separated. From 5.0 to 8.0 seconds the frame holds completely still on 月 with nothing else moving in the shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast but not neon colors, no dark or moody night grading. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「月、月、月亮」, using the reading ㄩㄝˋ for 月 both times and in the word. Speak the first 月 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 月亮 around 5.6 seconds during the still hold, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep the creak, bonk and brick clicks soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not appear as imagery. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 月: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

promptVersions.conceptZh: 「月」變成低重力的月球停車場；小賽車想停在下方橫畫，卻衝過頭，慢悠悠翻到上方橫畫，四輪朝天還在轉。
promptVersions.object: A solid indigo 月 sculpture serving as a miniature lunar parking structure, with its two interior horizontal strokes as parking ledges.
promptVersions.morph: Begin with the complete, correctly formed glyph. Its strokes remain fixed while the race car makes an exaggerated low-gravity hop between the two interior ledges; the car exits before the final isolated glyph hold.
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 不再讓月牙立起來或插入積木，而是直接利用「月」的兩條內橫做上下停車層。愛衝過頭的回力賽車遇到月球低重力，竟然翻上樓，輪子空轉；字形全程穩定，笑點不會遮住筆畫。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked frontal shot. Against a light warm-peach background, center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 月, rendered as a solid saturated-indigo sculpture occupying about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Preserve its standard four-stroke structure: the descending left stroke, the top horizontal turning into the right vertical hook, and two distinct interior horizontals. Use shallow extrusion so the interior horizontals can function as tiny parking ledges while the frontal silhouette remains unmistakable. This sculpture is the sole supporting object. Its subtly crater-dimpled surfaces and exaggerated lunar gravity make it a miniature moon playground; keep the dimples low contrast and away from stroke edges.

The lead is an original squeaky pull-back toy race car with a rounded tangerine plastic shell, tiny wheels and expressive googly eyes. It is confidently impatient, always braking too late. Keep it small enough to fit comfortably inside the glyph's openings. At 0.0–0.8 seconds, it sits near the left end of the lower interior horizontal, eyes confidently measuring the short parking space ahead. It rolls backward slightly to wind its spring, then releases. By 1.6 seconds it has raced across the ledge and overshot its intended stopping point. Its front wheels brake while its rear wheels keep spinning, launching it into one comically slow backward somersault within the open space between the two interior bars. At 2.6 seconds it lands upside down on the upper interior horizontal: all four wheels spin uselessly in the air, and its googly eyes swivel down toward the parking ledge it missed. Allow a short, silent reaction beat. A tiny springy chassis wiggle rights it; at 3.4 seconds it drops gently onto the lower ledge, finally stopping with all wheels planted. It gives one proud suspension bounce, then a last little spring release sends it rolling off the ledge and floating diagonally down and out of frame by 4.7 seconds. Keep its path within the openings or outside the sculpture, without crossing through strokes. The glyph never bends, moves or changes its construction.

By 4.8 seconds, the subtle surface dimples have softened away, leaving a crisp, uniformly indigo 月. Hold this single centered, uncropped glyph completely still through 8.0 seconds, with no other visible objects. Use bright, soft studio lighting, readable stroke gaps and gentle shadows.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「月、月、月亮」. Pronounce the first 月 at approximately 0.4 seconds, the second at 1.8 seconds, and 月亮 at 5.5–6.5 seconds during the clear final hold, using ㄩㄝˋ throughout. Leave natural pauses and stop after the word. Add quiet spring winding, rubber-wheel squeaks and a soft upside-down landing tap beneath the voice; use no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The sole on-screen writing is 月, with no subtitles, additional letters or numbers, logos, watermarks, clutter or flashing effects. All visible performance comes from the animated toy car and glyph sculpture.

concept.morph: the three peaks straighten into three vertical strokes standing on one horizontal base

promptVersions.conceptZh: 矮胖的戰鬥機器人用積木蓋山：左右兩根疊得剛剛好，他站上中間那根想再加一塊，結果中間柱子一直往上長，把他舉得超高，他在頂端手忙腳亂地揮手，最後滑桿溜下來；一條長積木從底下滑進來把三根接起來，變成「山」。
promptVersions.object: a stubby armored toy battle robot and stacks of chunky interlocking plastic bricks
promptVersions.morph: three brick columns rise with the middle one tallest and a long flat brick slides in beneath them, joining their feet into the base stroke of 山
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 第一次為「山」補上 prompt。用孩子喜歡的戰鬥機器人加樂高積木，笑點是「柱子自己一直長高，把蓋房子的人舉到天上」的尺寸落差，而這個動作本身就是中間那一豎變長的筆劃邏輯。語音詞選「火山」，火ㄏㄨㄛˇ、山ㄕㄢ都是單一讀音，且火是他已經學過的字。
promptVersions.promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light-cream background. A stubby, friendly toy battle robot with rounded armored shoulders and stompy feet is busy building with chunky interlocking plastic bricks, centered in frame. From 0.3 to 1.6 seconds he snaps together a short column of deep teal bricks on the left and a matching short column on the right, dusts off his hands, and nods with satisfaction. At 1.8 seconds he climbs onto the low middle stack to add one more brick on top, but the middle column keeps growing under his feet, brick after brick, lifting him far too high above his own building; he wobbles at the top, pedals his little arms in comic surprise, and freezes wide-eyed for a beat. 【8s Video Prompt】:
```text
An 8-second 3D educational animation centered on the Traditional Chinese character '手'. Against a soft, warm pastel teal background, a cute tiny blocky toy robot wearing an absurdly oversized wooden toy hand tries to wave enthusiastically (0:00-0:02). The top-heavy hand tips the little robot forward onto its belly with a harmless, funny wobble. In a comic surprise, the robot pops back onto its feet as the oversized toy hand detaches and fluidly transforms into glyph strokes (0:02-0:05): the angled thumb sweeps up to the left into the top diagonal stroke (撇), the blocky fingers line up into two horizontal parallel bars—a shorter top bar and a longer lower bar—and the wooden wrist extends straight down through the center, hooking sharply to the left at the base to form the vertical hook stroke (豎鉤). The strokes instantly fuse into the clean, vibrant coral-orange Traditional Chinese glyph '手', perfectly centered and occupying 70% of the frame height with generous margins (0:05-0:08). The glyph remains completely static for a solid 3-second hold. Warm, clear off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin voiceover pronounces '手' at 0:01, '手' at 0:03, and the everyday word '手套' cleanly at 0:05 during the static hold. High-contrast studio lighting with soft shadows; no on-screen text overlays, subtitles, or watermarks.
```

promptVersions.creativeAngle: 改用完整字形搭配手部動作，避免手指硬湊筆畫。自信的兔子變出過大手套，意外把帽子拍低遮眼，再小心掀帽揮手，形成清楚的魔術失誤笑點。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation with a locked, front-facing camera and a light warm cream background. Display one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph, 手, centered and uncropped from the opening frame, filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use a clean, standard educational typeface in saturated coral: a distinct gently sloping top left-falling stroke, two horizontal strokes with the lower one longer, and a central vertical hook ending toward the left. Keep every stroke stationary and clearly separated throughout.

In the open space beside the glyph stands an original cartoon magician rabbit with rounded lavender fur, expressive ears and an integral plum-colored top-hat costume. Its personality is grandly confident but endearingly clumsy. Its sole additional prop is a soft golden glove. Stage all action beside the glyph without touching or obscuring it. During 0.0–1.1 seconds, the rabbit proudly presents its tiny gloved paw and makes an elaborate magical flourish with its free paw. It pauses expectantly. During 1.1–2.3 seconds, the glove smoothly inflates to an absurd size, nearly as large as the rabbit. The rabbit stares at it, then attempts one magnificent wave. During 2.3–3.3 seconds, the floppy glove folds backward and gently pats its own top hat down over its eyes. The rabbit freezes with its ears sticking out sideways; add one soft fabric 'pof.' During 3.3–4.7 seconds, it carefully lifts the brim with the oversized glove, gives a tiny, deliberately cautious successful wave, and makes a quick sideways shuffle out of frame with its glove and hat. From 4.7–8.0 seconds, hold only the unchanged centered glyph completely still for 3.3 full seconds.

A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly: 「手、手、手套」. Speak the first 手 around 0.5 seconds, the second 手 around 1.6 seconds, and 手套 around 5.3 seconds during the unobstructed final hold, with natural pauses. Stop after the word. The vocabulary is audio only. Use gentle tactile sound effects below the voice and no music. Bright soft studio lighting, crisp stroke edges, no flashing effects, subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks or background clutter.

Create an exactly 8-second stylized toy animation in one locked, front-facing shot. On a light apricot background, center a large, correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 足, occupying approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. It is a shallow cobalt-blue relief with a thin sandy surface coating; its complete silhouette and open spaces are recognizable from the beginning. Use an accurate Traditional Chinese typeface as the fixed geometry, preserving every stroke and gap throughout.

At the lower left stands an original chunky coral-red toy fire engine with expressive windshield eyes and two unmistakably molded-plastic firefighter figures. Their oversized helmets, mitten hands and broad bare toy feet give them a cheerful, determined personality. The engine's flexible hose has a mischievously independent nozzle. The relief is the only additional object.

The startled toy lifts that foot, then comically hops once on the other foot while the nozzle follows the raised sole. Use a broad silent laughing expression and a soft rubber squeak; the engine gives an exaggerated windshield-eye double-take. Keep this action small and below the central strokes.

During 2.7–4.4 seconds, the firefighter plants both feet and firmly redirects the nozzle with help from the crewmate. A single controlled wash travels across the relief, removing the sandy coating and exposing uniformly saturated cobalt-blue strokes. The fixed top enclosure and precise lower stroke structure remain intact; water never becomes a stroke. The crew and hose retreat out of frame by 4.4 seconds, with all droplets settled.

Hold the finished 足 perfectly still, centered and unobstructed from 4.4–8.0 seconds. A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly: 「足、足、足球」. Schedule the first 足 around 4.5 seconds, the second around 5.4 seconds, and 足球 around 6.4–7.3 seconds, with natural short pauses. The vocabulary is audio only. Display only 足, with no subtitles, additional lettering, logos or watermarks. Use bright, soft lighting, restrained water sounds, no flashing effects and no music.

promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized stop-motion-like 3D animation with a locked frontal camera, a pale warm-peach background, soft lighting, and bright non-neon toy colors. The original lead is a proud, chunky coral toy fire engine with expressive windshield eyes, two tiny molded firefighter toy figures seated in its open cab, and a flexible hose with an independently mischievous nozzle. Its only supporting object is a centered upright reversible toy panel on an integrated vertical swivel. The front carries one large friendly cartoon eye with movable lids; the reverse carries the correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph「目」in saturated solid cobalt blue. Build that glyph as a tall closed rectangular outline with exactly two evenly spaced horizontal interior strokes connected to both sides, making three rectangular openings. The panel's pale reverse blends with the background, leaving the blue glyph visually dominant.

From 0.0–1.3 seconds, the engine waits beside the panel's lower-left corner, confidently aiming its hose toward the oversized eye. Its crew proudly lower their oversized transparent goggles. The eye looks toward the nozzle and opens expectantly. From 1.3–2.0 seconds, a gentle water stream starts, but the stubborn nozzle slowly curls backward. Give the engine a clear, puzzled sideways glance and a brief anticipation pause. From 2.0–3.2 seconds, the nozzle sprays both crew members' goggles instead! Water momentarily magnifies their painted toy eyes into enormous circles; both figures lean backward together while the engine makes an embarrassed little suspension dip. Keep the splash gentle and the reaction playful. The panel's eye blinks in amusement.

From 3.2–4.5 seconds, one crew figure closes the valve, straightens the now-limp hose, and uses its nozzle to nudge the panel's integrated swivel tab. The panel makes one smooth half-turn, revealing the already complete blue「目」on its reverse. The engine rolls out through the lower-left edge as the panel settles. From 4.5–8.0 seconds, hold the single finished glyph perfectly still, centered, unobstructed and uncropped, filling approximately 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins. Keep the eye illustration entirely hidden on the reverse throughout this final hold.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly「目、目、目光」, with 目 pronounced ㄇㄨˋ. Say the first 目 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.2 seconds with a short natural pause, and 目光 around 5.4 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly visible. Stop after the word. Add only quiet water patter and a soft swivel click beneath the voice; no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The single target glyph is the only on-screen writing: no subtitles, labels, logos, watermarks, extra text, clutter, or flashing effects.

【8s Video Prompt】:
```text
An 8-second 3D animated scene in a bright, clean 3D toy style. On a light mint backdrop, a chubby toy pig detective holding a giant round magnifying glass leans in to inspect a tiny, microscopic mechanical toy robot. From 0.0 to 2.0 seconds, the detective pig peers through the lens in comical focus. At 2.0 seconds, in a funny surprise payoff, the tiny toy robot springs straight up and morphs into a bold, solid dark-teal central hooked vertical stroke (亅), while its two micro lens accessories snap outward to the left and right into two clean diagonal dots (丶), cleanly constructing the single Traditional Chinese character "小". The pig detective's eyes widen behind the magnifying glass in a funny double-take recoil. By 5.0 seconds, the detective recedes into the background, leaving the character "小" perfectly centered, crisp, and upright, occupying 70% of the frame height against the clean background. From 5.0 to 8.0 seconds, the frame freezes completely for a static 3-second hold. Audio: A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks in clear Taiwanese Mandarin: "小、小、小豬". No on-screen text, subtitles, or heavy music.
```

promptVersions.morph: The correctly formed glyph remains unchanged; a smooth camera push enlarges its presentation for the final reading hold.
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 改用放大鏡看錯目標的鼻孔笑點，讓自信滿滿的豬探長先失手再找到小字；不再以機器人變形組字，完整保留「小」的豎鉤與左右筆畫。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation with warm toy-like materials and a pale apricot background. The lead is an original stout cartoon detective pig wearing a checked deerstalker hat, proudly carrying a magnifying glass almost as large as himself. His personality is comically overconfident but good-natured. The only additional scene element is one solid dark-teal Traditional Chinese glyph, 小, standing upright at the exact center. Use a standard, correctly formed glyph with a distinct central vertical stroke hooking left at its base and two separate, correctly positioned side strokes. Initially the complete glyph occupies 15% of frame height, visibly small beside the pig.

During the first 1.2 seconds, the pig stands to the left of the centered glyph, squints importantly, and hoists his enormous magnifying glass to investigate. From 1.2 to 2.8 seconds, he leans too eagerly: the heavy lens tips back against his soft snout, making two enormous nostrils fill the lens on the left side of the composition. Pause briefly on his crossed eyes as he realizes he is inspecting his own nose. A tiny rubbery squeak punctuates the mishap. Keep the glyph fully visible beside this action. From 2.8 to 3.5 seconds, he pulls his nose free, grins, and lowers the magnifying glass, finally spotting the little glyph directly. He proudly gestures toward it and shuffles out to the left with his glass. From 3.5 to 4.5 seconds, smoothly push the camera straight toward the stationary glyph, keeping its entire shape centered and uncropped. It reaches approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. From 4.5 through 8.0 seconds, hold the finished glyph completely still in a clean, front-facing composition. Its saturated solid strokes have crisp edges and clearly open gaps; keep shadows away from the stroke silhouette.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly: 「小、小、小豬」. Place the first 小 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 3.2 seconds, and 小豬 around 5.5 seconds during the clear final hold. Use the usual ㄒㄧㄠˇ reading. Finish after the word. Keep the gentle prop sound below the voice and use no music. The single 小 is the only visible writing throughout; the vocabulary is audio only. Use only the original animated pig and specified elements, with no subtitles, logos, watermarks, decorative text, clutter, or flashing effects.

From 0:02 to 0:05, to install the top-right branch, the robot triggers a coiled toy spring to launch a short navy wooden beam upward. Comically, the robot's arm catches on the spring lever, sending the robot launching upward into the air where it floats back down with a tiny head propeller, while the launched short beam snaps perfectly onto the upper-right side of the vertical stem. From 0:05 to 0:08, the completed target character "上" stands centered and perfectly uncropped, filling 70% of frame height with solid, high-contrast navy strokes. The final still hold lasts for 3 full seconds. Off-screen friendly Taiwanese Mandarin voice speaks: "上、上、上面". No on-screen vocabulary text, subtitles, watermarks, or extra text.

promptVersions.morph: The glyph remains correctly formed throughout; its upper shelf stages the mishap, and the warrior ultimately holds the shield above its head to demonstrate above.

promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation featuring the single Traditional Chinese glyph 上. Use a locked, straight-on camera, a light apricot background and soft, bright lighting. Center a saturated cobalt-blue, shallow-extruded 上 sculpture, fully uncropped and occupying about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Its correct silhouette consists of a long horizontal baseline, an upright rising from the baseline near its center, and a shorter horizontal extending only rightward from the upper portion of the upright; the upright continues visibly above that short horizontal. Preserve this silhouette throughout.

An original chunky toy warrior stands beside the glyph on the right, with obvious molded plastic joints, a rounded plain helmet, a foam sword and a round shield. Its puffed-out chest and extravagant gestures convey tremendous confidence and very little skill. Add no supporting characters or extra props. The short right-hand stroke has just enough shallow depth to function as a shelf, while its front face remains clearly readable.

During the first 1.5 seconds, the warrior carefully balances its shield on top of this short stroke, then proudly straightens up. After a brief self-satisfied pause, it performs an enormous sword salute. At about 2.2 seconds, the floppy sword accidentally nudges the shield: it tips off the shelf and lands horizontally on the warrior's helmet like an absurdly wide hat, sliding down to cover its eyes. Use a soft hollow toy clonk. The warrior freezes with its chest still puffed out, then peers beneath the shield with a sheepish sideways glance. By 4.6 seconds, it has tucked the sword under one arm and lifted the shield above its head with both hands, revealing a triumphant grin. Keep all acting beside the glyph; the falling shield travels outward, away from its strokes.

From 4.6 to 8.0 seconds, hold the entire composition still: the clear blue 上 remains centered, unobstructed and at full size, while the warrior holds its shield above its head at the right margin. A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly: 「上、上、上面」. Place the first 上 around 0.6 seconds, the second around 1.6 seconds, and 上面 around 5.5 seconds during the final clear hold, with natural pauses and no further speech. Use quiet toy sound effects and no music. Only 上 appears as on-screen writing; the vocabulary is audio only. No subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks, clutter or flashing effects.

【設計概念】：四格小田地的外圍田埂和十字小路組成「田」；愛耍帥的披風英雄跨田埂時，被自己的超長披風拉回原位，還蒙住了頭。
【8s Video Prompt】:
```text
Create an exactly 8-second animated toy comedy in a locked overhead orthographic view. Center a single square miniature field whose raised, saturated dark-green perimeter and intersecting paths form the correctly proportioned Traditional Chinese glyph 田. The continuous enclosure and full central vertical and horizontal dividers connect cleanly, creating four equal, spacious pale-sand rectangular plots. The glyph occupies about 70% of frame height, with generous margins, against a light warm-sand background. Keep the entire field centered and uncropped throughout; use shallow relief without perspective distortion or heavy shadows.

The lead is an original, proudly theatrical caped action-figure hero with visible toy joints, a rounded plum-colored suit, and a plain coral fabric cape three sizes too long. Give the figure a small scale relative to the field and an expressive, stylized face. The field is the sole supporting object.

At the opening, the hero stands at the central crossing, chest puffed out, preparing an extravagant leap across one narrow field path. The cape trails behind, its tip visibly trapped under the hero's rear boot. At 1.1 seconds, the hero launches a grand forward pose while that boot stays planted. The cape pulls taut and gently plops the figure back onto its bottom at the crossing. Its loose length then sails forward and flops completely over the hero's head. Pause briefly on the cape-covered lump; two little toy hands pat around searching for the opening. By 2.9 seconds, the hero lifts one corner, peeks out, and looks back at the guilty boot. The hero frees the cape, gathers the entire length into both arms, and succeeds with a modest little step over the same path. Then it briskly follows the central path out through the bottom margin, carrying the cape safely, fully exiting by 4.7 seconds. Use soft fabric motion and a gentle toy bounce for the single comic payoff.

From 4.7 to 8 seconds, hold completely still on the unobstructed 田. Its solid green enclosure and internal cross remain crisp and equally prominent; the four plain field interiors match the light background. Keep the strokes rigid throughout the action, with no added seams, decorative marks, or disconnected joins.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「田、田、田地」. Pronounce the first 「田」 around 0.3 seconds, the second around 1.0 seconds with a short pause between them, and 「田地」 around 5.4 seconds during the clear final hold. Use ㄊㄧㄢˊ for 田 and stop after the word. Accompany the cape flop with only a quiet fabric rustle; use no music. All imagery is stylized toy animation with soft lighting and bright, non-neon colors. The single target glyph 田 is the only on-screen text. Keep the vocabulary audio-only, without subtitles, additional lettering, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
```

The capsule rocks out of frame. Through 2.0 seconds, the creature makes two rubbery ricochets against the glyph's rigid lower side strokes, trying to bounce itself dry. promptVersions.promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animated educational video featuring the Traditional Chinese character '石'.

Scene Setup & Animation (0-5 seconds):
In a bright, warm studio setting with a clean pastel background, a cute boxy mechanical toy robot made of smooth stone blocks attempts to lift a heavy stone slab overhead. The square-shaped toy robot plops cleanly under the right side of the overhang, its eyes blinking in a funny, surprised reaction before its boxy body settles into the solid square '口' stroke. Together, the stone cliff overhang and the square toy body snap into the exact, beautifully proportioned Traditional Chinese glyph '石', filling approximately 70% of the frame height in a centered, uncropped composition with high-contrast, rich slate-blue strokes.

Final Hold (5-8 seconds):
The animation freezes completely into the solid, static glyph '石' against the clean, light background for a full 3-second clear hold without any visual distraction, text, subtitles, or clutter.

Audio & Narration:
Off-screen narration in a warm, friendly voice speaks in Taiwanese Mandarin: '石、石、石頭'. The audio pacing fits naturally within the 8 seconds, finishing while the glyph remains clearly displayed. Sound effects include light, playful toy clicking and a soft cartoon thud, with no loud startling noises or background music overpowering the speech.

promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated toy-theater clip with warm pastel lighting and a light cream background. A stylized cartoon pig detective wears a tiny felt detective hat and investigates a centered toy bowl of cooked rice. Use one coherent detective theme, rounded toy materials, and a fixed frontal camera with generous margins.

From 0.0–1.8 seconds, the pig leans in from beside the bowl and carefully sweeps a magnifying glass over the rice. One sticky rice grain attaches to his snout. He pauses solemnly, unaware of it. From 1.8–3.2 seconds, he brings the lens toward his snout: the attached grain suddenly looks enormous through the glass. His eyes widen and his hat gives one small springy hop. He lowers the lens, revealing the tiny grain still stuck there—the entire comic payoff. Keep the reaction gentle and silent.

From 3.2–4.3 seconds, the pig backs out sideways while the rice bowl smoothly descends into the stage, revealing a complete, flat, saturated vermilion Traditional Chinese glyph 米 standing centered behind it. Use a clear standard printed form, with no grain textures or decorative stroke substitutions. By 4.3 seconds all props and the pig have cleared the frame. Hold only 米 perfectly still and unobstructed through 8.0 seconds, filling approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The ONLY spoken line is exactly "米、米、米飯". Say the first 米 around 0.7 seconds, the second around 2.1 seconds, and 米飯 around 5.2 seconds while the finished glyph is fully visible. Allow natural pauses. Silent pronunciation directions, never spoken or displayed: 米 = ㄇㄧˇ = mǐ; 米飯 = mǐ fàn. Use the same mǐ reading for all three occurrences. Stop after 米飯. No other dialogue or music. Display only the single target glyph 米; no vocabulary text, subtitles, pronunciation labels, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.

The top beam gives a smug little eyebrow lift while the bottom beam's feet begin to wobble. At 1.5–2.2 seconds, hold a brief, readable anticipation: every face looks down toward those wobbling feet. At 2.2–3.0 seconds, the tower concertinas into a comically flat stack, with six surprised faces peeking out in a vertical row. The rice grain settles gently on top like an enormous cushion, then rolls off the stack and exits the frame. Use a soft plastic clatter and a tiny squeak, never a startling crash.

At 3.0–4.6 seconds, the determined squad recovers through coordinated movement: the long vertical beam rises upright, the horizontal beam slides across its middle, two short beams rotate into the separate upper diagonal strokes, and two longer beams extend into the lower left-falling and right-falling strokes. Follow the exact geometry of a standard Traditional Chinese printed 米: two separate inward-sloping upper strokes above the horizontal, a central horizontal and vertical cross, and the long lower spreading 撇 and 捺. Preserve the characteristic spacing, junctions, and tapered stroke ends; do not make a symmetrical asterisk or four dots around a cross.

By 4.6 seconds, their faces, feet, studs, and seams have smoothly receded, leaving one clean, flat, solid vermilion 米. Hold this correctly formed glyph completely still and unobstructed from 4.6 through 8.0 seconds, centered at approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. The rice grain and all separate objects are now out of view.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin. The exact and only spoken line is "米、米、米飯". Pronounce the first 米 at approximately 0.5 seconds, the second 米 at 2.0 seconds, and 米飯 at 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. concept.hook: 胖胖的玩具飛機在原地猛催油門、機身抖個不停卻黏在地上；它洩氣地垂下機鼻，這時螺旋槳終於轉對邊，它整台倒著咻一聲飛出去。

promptVersions.creativeAngle: 接上孩子喜歡的戰鬥機與飛行英雄：笑點是「引擎全開卻原地發抖，最後倒著飛走」的方向錯誤。飛的兩組羽狀筆畫最容易被動畫畫錯，所以字體全程不動。語音詞「飛機」，機ㄐㄧ已經學過，兩字都只有一種讀音。
promptVersions.promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid warm ivory background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 飛 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep sky blue, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the tall hooked central stroke and the two matching feather-like groups on the upper left and right stay clearly separated, with every stroke and dot readable. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. In front of its lower right stands a chubby toy propeller plane with googly eyes and stubby wings. From 0.7 seconds it revs hard: the propeller blurs, the whole fuselage shudders and rattles in place, little puffs of effort pop from the tail - and it does not move a single centimetre. The shaking builds until 2.4 seconds, then stops dead. The plane's nose droops forward in disappointment and its googly eyes settle at different heights. Beat. At 3.3 seconds the propeller suddenly spins the other way and the plane shoots backwards out of frame to the right with a cheerful whoosh, tail first, googly eyes spinning. At 4.2 seconds one small screw drops from where it stood, bounces twice and rolls out of shot. From 4.6 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 飛 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「飛、飛、飛機」, using the reading ㄈㄟ for 飛 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 飛 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 飛機 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 飛: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

promptVersions.conceptZh: 消防車想把不聽話的水管舉高，水管卻朝下噴水，把整台車變成空中消防車；隊員終於合作控制方向，飛一小圈後平穩落地。
promptVersions.object: An original chunky toy fire engine with two molded toy firefighter crew members and a mischievous flexible hose.
promptVersions.morph: Keep 飛 as a complete, solid-colored textbook glyph throughout. The hose turns the fire engine into a briefly flying vehicle beside the glyph, illustrating its meaning without altering its strokes.
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 把原先飛機倒退起飛的笑點，改成消防水管反客為主：隊員努力抬水管，結果水管把整台消防車抬上天。以實際離地飛行表現「飛」，完整字形全程保留，避免複雜筆畫變形或混淆。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second original stylized 3D toy animation in one locked, front-facing landscape shot. On a light warm cream background, display the single Traditional Chinese glyph 飛 centered and uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height, with generous margins. Render it in saturated cobalt blue using a correctly formed standard Taiwanese textbook glyph, with crisp, clearly separated strokes and open internal spaces. Preserve this exact glyph silhouette throughout; the animation illustrates its meaning beside it.

In the roomy left margin, stage a chunky coral-red toy fire engine with expressive windshield eyes, two visibly molded toy firefighter figures seated in its open cab, and one flexible hose attached to its side. These are original unbranded toy designs. The engine is eager and overconfident; its hose is cheekily independent. Keep their entire performance outside the glyph silhouette, with no additional props.

At 0.0–1.3 seconds, the engine plants its wheels proudly while both crew members pull together to point the hose upward. The hose bends stubbornly back down. Their arms stretch forward; the engine squints with determination. At 1.3–1.8 seconds, they give one final tug, freeze hopefully, and watch the nozzle curl straight toward the floor. At 1.8 seconds, a soft, compact water jet begins. Instead of lifting the nozzle, its downward thrust lifts the entire fire engine clear of the floor! By 2.5 seconds, all four wheels are dangling and spinning uselessly in the air. Both crew members look down together, then back at the hose; the engine's proud expression becomes a wide-eyed round-mouthed surprise. Keep the ascent slow enough to read, with a clearly separated floor shadow showing actual flight.

From 2.5–3.9 seconds, the crew cooperate to angle the nozzle. The engine makes one small, smooth airborne loop entirely within the left margin, now grinning as it learns to steer. From 3.9–4.6 seconds, they ease the jet down and land gently. The hose curls smugly over the cab while the two crew members sink back into their seats in relief. All water disappears by 4.6 seconds. Hold the complete composition absolutely still from 4.6 through 8.0 seconds: the large centered 飛 remains dominant, and the tiny parked engine rests quietly in the left margin. Never move, stretch, rotate, obscure, or crop the glyph.

Use rounded toy materials, soft studio shadows, bright non-neon colors, and clear visual separation. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「飛、飛、飛機」. Say the first 飛 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 2.9 seconds, and 飛機 around 5.6 seconds during the still hold, with natural pauses and the reading ㄈㄟ throughout. Stop speaking after 飛機. Add only quiet rubber squeaks, a gentle water hiss, and a soft landing sound beneath the voice; no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The sole visible writing is 飛, with no subtitles, labels, numerals, logos, watermarks, unrelated text, clutter, or flashing effects.

Use standard textbook proportions: the 雨 radical on top, with its four inner dots clearly separated, sits above the 电 component whose bottom stroke hooks upward. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. At its base slumps a small boxy toy robot, completely out of power: knees folded, arms hanging like wet noodles, visor dim and drooping. From 0.6 to 1.8 seconds nothing happens except one arm slowly sliding further down, which is the joke. At 2.0 seconds a chunky cartoon battery, almost as big as he is, rolls in from the left, bumps his heel, wobbles upright and clicks into a socket on his back. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「電、電、電池」, using the reading ㄉㄧㄢˋ for 電 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 電 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 電池 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. promptVersions.conceptZh: 電讓電風扇轉動；發條樂團想吹風耍帥，卻被風吹出一連串走音與翻倒。
promptVersions.object: An original wind-up animal trio with cymbals, a squeeze-bulb horn and a drum, plus one small electric fan.
promptVersions.morph: The complete glyph remains a stationary, solid-colored teaching sculpture; an electric fan demonstrates its meaning through the band's physical comedy.
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 改用電風扇引發樂器連環失控，取代電池充電笑點。自信的發條樂團先被風吹得敲錯、吹錯、翻倒，再調低風速成功合奏；字形全程完整，不拿筆畫當道具。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, front-facing shot. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 電, occupying about 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Use a standard Taiwanese textbook glyph as the exact silhouette: clearly separated dots in the upper 雨 component and a fully legible lower portion with its turning hook. Render every stroke in solid saturated cobalt blue against a pale peach background, with soft studio lighting. The complete glyph is present from the first frame and stays stationary, unobstructed and uncropped throughout.

Along the lower foreground, safely below the glyph, stage an original miniature wind-up animal band: a bossy wooden duck cymbal player, an earnest wooden mouse with a squeeze-bulb horn, and a round wooden bear drummer. Visible brass winding keys establish their mechanical toy identity. Their instruments belong to the band; the only additional object is a small electric fan with a guarded rotor, an integrated speed lever and a short power cord leading offscreen along the floor. Keep these miniature objects clearly separated from the character's strokes.

At the opening, the duck confidently raises its cymbals and gestures for a grand entrance. At 0.8 seconds it nudges the fan's speed lever with its foot, expecting a glamorous breeze. The electrically powered rotor accelerates smoothly; the trio proudly lean into the airflow for a brief anticipation beat. From 1.5 to 3.1 seconds, deliver one readable domino mishap: the breeze tips the duck's raised cymbals together with a soft clash; its backward wobble presses the mouse's horn bulb for a ridiculous little honk; the mouse's horn bell nudges the bear's drum, which tips onto its side and gently rolls the round bear backward onto its bottom. Show each contact distinctly. The duck freezes with an astonished open beak while the bear calmly taps the sideways drum once. No sparks or flashing light.

From 3.2 to 4.6 seconds, the duck sheepishly lowers the fan speed, the bear rights its drum, and the trio successfully play one tiny coordinated flourish, then bow. Their winding keys continue turning independently of the electric fan, making the distinction clear. By 4.8 seconds all action has settled. Hold the centered 電 completely clear and still through 8.0 seconds; the band rests quietly below it and the fan rotor stops smoothly. Use bright painted wood, rounded forms and expressive toy faces, with an uncluttered composition and no camera movement.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「電、電、電風扇」. Say the first 電 at approximately 0.2 seconds, the second at 1.0 seconds, and 電風扇 naturally between 5.3 and 6.5 seconds while the glyph is clearly held. Use ㄉㄧㄢˋ consistently. Stop speaking after the word. Keep the clash, honk, drum tap and fan hum gentle and below the voice; use no background music. The vocabulary is audio only. The single glyph 電 is the only on-screen writing: no subtitles, labels, other characters, logos or watermarks.

Use standard textbook proportions: the 竹 radical on top, its two halves evenly matched, sits above the 夭 component with its sweeping left stroke and long right stroke clearly separated. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Beside its lower right stands a stern toy robot referee with a flat visor face, a tiny whistle and an even tinier cap, arms folded, absolutely determined to stay serious. From 0.7 seconds a tiny cartoon penguin waddles across the bottom of frame on perfectly flat, perfectly empty ground - and slips anyway, feet flying up, landing softly on its back with its flippers sticking straight up. It stays exactly like that. The referee's visor stays rigid. Beat. At 2.3 seconds a single crack of a grin appears at the corner of his visor; he clamps it flat again and stiffens his arms. At 3.0 seconds the penguin waggles one flipper. The referee loses it completely: from 3.2 to 4.3 seconds his whole body shakes with silent laughter, his visor curving into an enormous grin, his tiny cap bouncing off his head and landing on the penguin's tummy. By 4.7 seconds both of them have wobbled happily out of frame to the right. From 4.8 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 笑 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「笑、笑、大笑」, using the reading ㄒㄧㄠˋ for 笑 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 笑 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 大笑 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 笑: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

promptVersions.conceptZh: 科學家老鼠想吹平冒泡的實驗液，卻吹出一副比自己還寬的泡泡鬍子；鬍子搔到鼻尖，牠忍不住笑開了。
promptVersions.object: A meticulous, bespectacled cartoon lab mouse with one molded twin-chamber bubbling beaker
promptVersions.morph: The complete glyph remains intact while an oversized foam moustache makes the mouse demonstrate laughter beside it.
promptVersions.creativeAngle: 改用老鼠親自操作失手的泡泡實驗：越想吹平泡沫，鬍子反而越大，最後被自己的鬍子逗笑。以動作呈現「笑」的意思，字形全程完整，避免道具變筆畫造成誤讀。
promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, front-facing shot. On a pale peach background, place the single Traditional Chinese glyph 笑 precisely at frame center, uncropped and approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Render its strokes in solid saturated raspberry, using a correctly formed standard Taiwanese textbook glyph: the clear 竹 radical above 夭, with every stroke and internal gap preserved. Keep this glyph fully visible, stationary and unchanged throughout. All characters and objects are original animated designs, with rounded toy-like materials and soft studio lighting.

In the open lower-left margin, stage a small, bespectacled cartoon scientist mouse with oversized round ears, a molded lavender laboratory coat and an enthusiastically meticulous personality. Its sole separate prop is one molded twin-chamber beaker, both chambers visibly bubbling with pastel liquid. Keep the entire gag outside the glyph’s silhouette, with enough room to read the mouse’s expressions.

At 0.0–1.4 seconds, the mouse scrutinizes the rising foam, proudly straightens its spectacles, then carefully blows across the beaker to flatten the bubbles. Pause briefly as the foam seems to settle. At 1.4–2.7 seconds, the chambers gently fizz over together: two connected curls of foam rise onto its upper lip, making an absurdly wide, curled moustache. The mouse goes cross-eyed at it and gives one determined little puff; the moustache balloons even wider. At 2.7–4.0 seconds, its curled tips bend inward and tickle the mouse’s nose. The mouse scrunches its face, then breaks into unmistakable silent laughter, eyes squeezed into happy crescents and belly bouncing. The foam collapses into the beaker with a soft plop. At 4.0–4.6 seconds, the mouse beams at the now-settled liquid, proudly hugs its successful experiment and scampers off the left edge with the beaker. From 4.6–8.0 seconds, hold completely still on the clean, centered 笑 alone for 3.4 full seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「笑、笑、笑臉」. Pronounce 笑 as ㄒㄧㄠˋ each time, including within 笑臉. Place the first 笑 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 3.0 seconds, and 笑臉 around 5.6 seconds during the unobstructed final hold. Use natural pauses and stop after the word. The mouse’s laughter is visual only; keep bubbling and the foam plop soft beneath the narration, with no music. Only 笑 appears as writing anywhere in the image; the vocabulary stays audio only. Maintain a bright, uncluttered composition without subtitles, labels, logos, watermarks, flashing effects or blown-out highlights.

promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D cartoon animation in one locked-off frontal wide shot. Against a light butter-yellow background, place one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 戰 at the center, filling approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Give its flat front a saturated deep blue finish and minimal extrusion. Use an accurate standard Traditional Chinese textbook glyph: 單 on the left and 戈 on the right, preserving the two distinct 口 forms at the top of 單, every interior gap, and the separate strokes, dot and hook of 戈. Keep the entire glyph stationary, sharp, uncropped and unobstructed throughout.

In the open lower-left margin, stage an original stout cartoon detective pig with a checked deerstalker hat, tiny determined eyebrows and an enormously oversized magnifying glass. Design the pig with rounded animated proportions and springy cartoon movement. The magnifying glass is his only prop; its lens is approximately as wide as his body. Leave enough space beside the glyph for the entire gag without crossing its silhouette.

At the opening, the self-important detective plants his feet and lifts the magnifying glass like a mighty battle shield, puffing out his chest toward an imaginary opponent off-screen left. By 1.2 seconds he has achieved a wonderfully grand defensive pose. Pause briefly as his proud smile turns into a strained wobble: the shield is much too heavy. From 1.8 to 3.1 seconds its weight pulls his arms downward, his feet make two frantic little recovery steps, and he plops gently onto his padded bottom. The glass rim settles upright on the floor directly between his snout and the camera. His eyes remain visible above the rim while the lens optically enlarges his pink snout into two enormous round nostrils. Keep this optical effect entirely within his side of the frame, away from the lettering. Hold the astonished nostril close-up for a short beat; he blinks, notices the ridiculous result, and gives a sheepish little grin. At 3.7 seconds he succeeds by lowering the oversized glass flat and sliding it away with both forelegs, then proudly shuffles after it. Both exit completely by 4.7 seconds. Hold only the complete centered 戰 perfectly still from 4.7 through 8.0 seconds.

Use soft studio lighting, bright non-neon colors and clear silhouettes. The miniature mock battle should feel playful and harmless. Add only a soft wobble squeak and a quiet padded plop, kept below the narration. A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「戰、戰、戰車」. Pronounce the first 戰 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.5 seconds, and 戰車 around 5.6 seconds, using ㄓㄢˋ consistently and natural pauses. Stop speaking after the word. Keep the finished glyph clearly visible during the word. The vocabulary is audio only. The single 戰 is the only on-screen writing; use no subtitles, logos, watermarks, additional text, clutter, flashing effects or background music.

promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one continuous locked frontal shot. On a light warm cream background, display the single Traditional Chinese glyph 龍 centered and uncropped, occupying approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Render it in saturated deep teal using an accurately formed standard Taiwanese textbook typeface, with crisp strokes and clearly open internal spaces. Keep its geometry, position and color fixed throughout. Use a wide composition with a separate performance area in the right margin, leaving every stroke unobstructed.

The lead is an original, extravagantly confident caped action-figure hero: obvious molded plastic joints, oversized mitten hands, a round orange helmet and a plain lavender suit without an emblem. His soft coral cape is three sizes too long. Its trailing hem has a broad, rounded dinosaur-snout profile, two embroidered eyes and a few soft triangular fabric spikes, all integrated into the same cape. There are no additional characters or props.

At 0.0–1.3 seconds, the tiny hero stands proudly beside the lower right of 龍, curls his hands into dinosaur claws and takes an exaggerated preparatory breath. He throws his arms up for a magnificent dinosaur pose. At 1.3–2.5 seconds, that flourish whips the enormous cape forward over his own helmet: FLOMP. The dinosaur-shaped hem lands over his face, its absurdly long soft snout drooping almost to his feet. Pause briefly on the ridiculous silhouette, with his little claw hands still frozen in their grand pose. At 2.5–3.3 seconds, he feels along the unexpected snout, lifts its tip and gives a delighted little body bounce as he discovers the puppet. At 3.3–4.7 seconds, he intentionally makes the fabric dinosaur perform one grand, slow nod, then proudly shuffles out through the right edge with the cape gathered in his hands. Finish all movement by 4.7 seconds. From 4.7 to 8.0 seconds, hold completely still on the clean, centered 龍 alone.

Use bright, softly lit toy materials and readable silhouettes. The gag comes from the oversized cape swallowing the hero's carefully rehearsed pose, followed by his resourceful recovery. Keep the cloth action confined to the side performance area. No camera motion, flashing effects or decorative clutter.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「龍、龍、恐龍」. Pronounce 龍 as ㄌㄨㄥˊ. Speak the first 龍 at approximately 0.3–0.9 seconds, the second at 1.1–1.7 seconds, and 恐龍 at 5.4–6.4 seconds during the final stationary glyph hold. Allow natural pauses and stop after the word. Add only a quiet cloth flop and soft plastic footsteps beneath the narration; no music or other vocalizations. The vocabulary is audio only. The only visible writing is 龍, with no subtitles, extra glyphs, logos or watermarks.

Use saturated solid plum-purple strokes with shallow rounded depth and a crisp, conventional printed silhouette: a narrow 王 on the left and 元 on the right, including its distinct left-falling stroke and curved hooked right stroke. It proudly balances there, eyes fixed on 王, then crouches much too deeply for such a short jump. promptVersions.promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, front-facing shot. On a pale warm apricot drawing surface, center one Traditional Chinese target glyph, 畫, in saturated solid indigo, sized to occupy approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Build its geometry from a correct Taiwanese textbook glyph master, preserving all intended joins, openings, and stroke spacing. Initially, every stroke is present except the final bottom horizontal stroke. That last stroke will be drawn during the action; use the master to determine its exact position, thickness, length, and endpoints. Keep the teaching subject centered and uncropped throughout.

The original lead is a proudly determined mint-green rubber dinosaur with enormous soft feet, comically tiny arms, and a bouncy rubber tail. Its only supporting prop is one indigo crayon, lying beside the starting point of the missing bottom stroke. Present the scene as a shallow drawing stage so its feet and the crayon can contact the drawing surface while the lettering remains square to camera.

From 0.0–1.6 seconds, the dinosaur bends toward the crayon, concentrating fiercely. Its tiny arms paddle and miss twice, while its enormous toes are already touching the crayon. It looks from its useless little hands down to its toes and pauses in sudden realization. From 1.6–2.4 seconds, it proudly grips the crayon between two toes and raises its chin like a master artist. From 2.4–3.7 seconds, it presses the tip to the correct starting point and pushes sideways. Its oversized foot slides farther than expected: both tiny arms windmill, its rubber body stretches, and it lands softly on its bottom while the toe-held crayon smoothly completes the exact final horizontal stroke. The controlled crayon trace produces one clean, straight line with no stray marks. Keep this action below the other strokes. A quiet rubber squeak accompanies the landing.

From 3.7–4.8 seconds, the seated dinosaur looks up at the perfectly completed 畫, glances proudly at its giant foot, and gives a delighted tiny-arm victory pose. promptVersions.creativeAngle: 用拍照框不進去把高矮差距變成看得見的問題，三次嘗試的節奏很清楚，結尾長頸鹿趴下來遷就朋友也很可愛。高十畫、上中下三段堆疊，中間兩個口最容易畫糊，字體靜止並要求各段分明。語音詞「高手」，手ㄕㄡˇ已學過，兩字都是單一讀音。
promptVersions.promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 高 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep teal blue, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the small top stroke and dot, the 口 beneath them, and the lower section with its own 口 inside stay clearly separated as three stacked bands, none of them merging. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Along its base a tall toy giraffe and a short boxy toy robot shuffle together in front of a tiny tripod camera, getting ready for a photo. At 1.0 second they pose: the giraffe's head is entirely out of frame above, leaving only legs and neck. They regroup. At 1.9 seconds the giraffe crouches to help and now its body completely hides the robot, whose small hand waves helplessly from behind a knee. They regroup again, both looking at the camera for guidance. Beat. At 2.9 seconds the giraffe simply lies all the way down on its belly and rests its chin on the floor, and the robot trots over and presses his cheek right beside it - and at last the two faces sit side by side, exactly the same height, both beaming. They hold the pose happily until 4.4 seconds, then amble out of frame to the left with the tripod. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 高 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「高、高、高手」, using the reading ㄍㄠ for 高 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 高 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 高手 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 高: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.
